summary: Final dosing readout for Nimbravelle Medicines Inc. The cosolvent-rich vehicle failed the dilution challenge despite acceptable undiluted behavior; the selected dispersed approach requires explicit redispersion and withdrawal controls.

slides.title: NM-12: dispersed dosing after dilution failure
slides.subtitle: {{PRJ0112:project_id}} | {{PRJ0112:lims_id}} | Nimbravelle Medicines Inc | Lena Patel | 09/28/2020 | Durnesswick Laboratories Inc

slides.title: Dosing decision
bullets: Nimbravelle Medicines Inc selected a dispersed dosing approach.
The cosolvent-rich vehicle failed the dilution challenge.
Handling controls now matter as much as preparation appearance.

slides.title: Equilibrium capacity is only part of the choice
slides.notes: Target loading 10 mg/mL. This chart does not measure dilution behavior or particle-size distribution.

slides.title: From screen to handoff
bullets: Opened 07/06/2020; interim review 08/17/2020; final handoff 09/28/2020.
Julia Carver led formulation development; Miguel Serrano supported the formulation set.
Lena Patel prepared the transfer interpretation.

slides.title: Why the clear route was attractive
bullets: PEG400/water gave a clear solution at screen loading.
The undiluted preparation was stable in the standing observation.
bullets_right: Those observations apply to the screen condition.
The dilution challenge failed, so the undiluted row cannot establish dosing suitability.

slides.title: Dilution failure: operational consequence
bullets: Dilution removes the solvent environment supporting the preparation.
Precipitation makes a solution-based withdrawal instruction unreliable.
Increasing cosolvent without a new dilution assessment would repeat the selection error.
slides.notes: Formulation interpretation, not a measured precipitation-rate model; no numerical dilution dataset is supplied.

slides.title: Shortlist logic
bullets: Methylcellulose showed a fine suspension that redispersed on shaking.
The surfactant/PEG mixture also redispersed, with a different excipient burden.
bullets_right: The aqueous surfactant mixture and citrate buffer showed caking.
A redispersible screen row is a starting point; the outcome does not identify a locked dispersed recipe.

slides.title: What changes at the dosing bench
bullets: Mix before withdrawal; do not sample only the clear upper layer.
Keep mixing instructions beside the dose calculation.
Check that settled material returns to a uniform dispersion before continuing.

slides.title: Recipe card must answer dosing questions

rows: Persistent cake or failure to redisperse

slides.title: Concentration and loading language
bullets: Use mg/mL for dose concentration and specify total suspended material.
Use weight percent for excipient loading where appropriate.
Do not label a dispersion a solution because it looks uniform after mixing.

slides.title: Transfer responsibilities
bullets: Miguel Serrano: attach observations and preparation sequence.
Julia Carver: approve the dilution-failure interpretation.
bullets_right: Lena Patel: make redispersion and withdrawal steps usable.
Nimbravelle Medicines Inc: align the approach with the exposure dosing plan.

slides.title: Screen suitability at use
bullets: Inspect after standing and again after resuspension.
Document cake remaining attached to the container.
Escalate a changed material lot or dose concentration before treating the recipe as equivalent.

slides.title: Limits of this final readout
bullets: The ladder reports equilibrium capacity and short-term physical behavior.
Quantitative dilution curves and dose-uniformity measurements are not supplied.
Process validation and shelf-life need separate work packages.

slides.title: Closeout: accept the handling tradeoff
bullets: A clear concentrate did not survive dilution.
The dispersed route accepts mixing and withdrawal discipline for a workable dosing approach.
Next scale gate: reproducibility at the intended preparation volume.
